y1: John had said the Messiah would judge with an ax and fire (3:10–12). But Jesus was healing the sick and eating with sinners. In prison, John was confused.
y2: Jesus answers by combining Isaiah 35 and 61: the blind see, the lame walk, and the Gospel is preached to the poor. And He says: “Blessed is he who doesn't stumble because of Me!”
y3: Right after John's question, Jesus praises him, saying, 'Among those born of women there has not risen anyone greater than John.' Doubt is not the opposite of faith. John took his doubt and went to Jesus. That is faith.
y5: Jesus compares that generation to children refusing to play: they won't join a wedding game or a funeral game. John fasted, and they said, 'He has a demon'; Jesus ate and drank, and they said, 'He is a glutton.'
y6: Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum, which saw the most miracles, did not repent. Jesus sighs over these cities. Those who see much bear much responsibility.
y7: “Wisdom is proved right by her actions” (11:19). Truth is proven by fruit, not by people's criticism. This connects to the words in chapter 7, “by their fruit you will recognize them.”
y9: “I thank You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that You have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children.” At the moment of rejection, Jesus gives thanks instead of complaining.
y10: “No one knows the Son except the Father. No one knows the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son desires to reveal Him.” The way to know God is opened only through Jesus.
y11: Knowing God is not something 'achieved' by studying, but something God 'shows'. Therefore, a humble person has the advantage. Knowledge is valuable, but proud knowledge blinds the eyes.
y13: “Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened.” At that time, the Pharisees added hundreds of rules to the Law, crushing the people (23:4).
y14: Jesus doesn't make the burden disappear; He changes the yoke. A yoke is carried by two oxen together. When we carry it with Jesus, He takes the weight, and we 'learn' from Him. “I am gentle and humble in heart; take My yoke upon you and learn from Me.”
y15: In the Old Testament, 'rest' refers to the Sabbath and the Promised Land. The very next chapter, 12, is about a Sabbath dispute. Jesus is the Lord of the Sabbath who gives the true rest of the Sabbath.
verse: “Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest. Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.”
prayer: Jesus, thank You for not scolding John when he doubted, and for calling the weary to 'come to Me'. Let me lay down the heavy burden in my heart and take Your yoke. Let me find true rest by learning from You, who are gentle and humble. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: Gospel. It is the fulfillment of Isaiah 61:1. Jesus also read these words in the synagogue in Nazareth (Luke 4:18). The sign of the Messiah was not military power, but restoration and joyful news.
d1: little child. It refers to people without knowledge or status. The disciples were also like 'little children' who had not graduated from the Law school. It connects to the words in 18:3, 'unless you turn and become as little children'.
d2: yoke. In Jewish writings, the 'yoke of the Law' meant submitting to a rabbi's teaching. Jesus gives His own teaching as a yoke. As a carpenter, Jesus might have made yokes Himself.
d3: rest. It is not just stopping work, but breathing again and being restored in God. It is a quote from Jeremiah 6:16, 'you will find rest for your souls'.
